key_insight: A common benchmark—one exact sample per second—makes photonic simulation limits comparable and shows that source coherence can increase classical simulation cost.
engineering_relevance: Hardware speedups shift the simulability frontier modestly, while algorithms that reduce exponential scaling can have a larger impact.
method: Define the frontier using exact output sampling, up to floating-point rounding, on fixed hardware.
Benchmark photonic-engines GPU samplers across single-photon, entangled, coherent-superposition and squeezed-light inputs.
Validate each sampler against an independent simulator sharing no code.
evidence_signal: On one NVIDIA H100, the frontier was 38.3 single photons and 31.0 entangled photons from one emitter; a fitted timing model estimated 41.5 squeezed inputs with mean photon number 0.5.
watch_item: These exact-sampling frontiers depend on the chosen hardware, algorithms and optical configuration; they do not establish limits for approximate classical sampling.
paper_title: The simulability frontiers of photonic quantum computing
